title: Factors influencing teachers’ adoption of artificial intelligence tools in K-12 education
venue: International Journal of Applied Resilience and Sustainability
extended_summary:
This paper asks what factors influence teachers’ adoption of artificial intelligence tools in K-12 education. It is motivated by the uneven uptake of AI-based instructional tools in schools, despite rapid growth in generative AI, intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, and other AI-supported teaching applications. The authors frame adoption as shaped by technological, pedagogical, psychological, institutional, and ethical conditions rather than by technical capability alone.

The study is a systematic literature review conducted under PRISMA 2020 guidelines. It synthesized 47 empirical and theoretical studies published between 2019 and 2025 from major databases including Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed. The review focuses on teachers in K-12 settings, including in-service and pre-service educators, and considers established acceptance models such as TAM, UTAUT, and TPACK, along with newer constructs such as AI literacy, trust, AI readiness, human-AI collaboration, and ethical AI.

The main conclusion is that teachers’ intention to use AI tools is most strongly shaped by perceived usefulness, ease of use, professional development, institutional support, trust, and ethical concerns. The review also emphasizes that successful AI adoption in schools depends on alignment with pedagogy, curriculum, and policy, as well as continuous training and organizational readiness. It highlights emerging AI applications such as lesson planning, automated grading, adaptive learning, chatbots, and smart classroom systems, but argues that adoption is constrained when these tools are not transparent, trustworthy, or well integrated into school workflows.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic literature review using PRISMA 2020, but it is not a primary causal study and does not estimate intervention effects. The evidence base is synthesized narratively from heterogeneous studies, so credibility is moderate rather than high.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper identifies potentially important adoption drivers for AI use in schools, but it does not demonstrate measured student or teacher outcome gains from an intervention. Its impact is therefore informative for implementation and policy, but the empirical effect on practice is unclear.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of AI adoption factors for K-12 teachers across AI-supported teaching tools, including generative AI, intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, automated grading, smart classroom systems, and AI-based professional development.

finding.finding_summary: This PRISMA-based systematic literature review synthesizes 47 studies on teacher adoption of AI tools in K-12 settings rather than testing a single intervention effect. The review concludes that adoption is strongly shaped by institutional support, policy alignment, professional development, AI literacy, ethical concerns, and organizational readiness; it does not report a pooled effect size or experimental outcome estimate.
finding.measure: Narrative synthesis of adoption factors and implementation conditions across 47 reviewed studies

finding.finding_summary: The review reports that teachers are more willing to adopt AI when it reduces workload, especially for lesson planning, grading, feedback, and routine instructional tasks. These benefits are described as increasing perceived usefulness and effort expectancy, but no pooled effect size is reported because the paper is a qualitative synthesis of prior studies.
finding.measure: Reported teacher perceptions of workload reduction, usefulness, and ease of use across reviewed studies
